text:
rachel: weird bug in examples/node-starter: request_id is being reused across retry attempts, making it impossible to tell which attempt failed. also log level jumps to WARN on auth retry and hides debug traces.

devin: hmm, can you paste a raw snippet?

rachel: sure: `2026-09-12T15:02:11Z DEBUG http.request path=/chat request_id=rid-8f7a attempt=1 auth_status=401` then `2026-09-12T15:02:11Z WARN  http.request path=/chat request_id=rid-8f7a attempt=2 auth_status=401 token_retry=true`

rachel: note same rid across attempt=1 and attempt=2. expected a new request id per network attempt or at least attempt appended.

alex: that's bad. retry middleware probably clones the request context without regenerating reqid. Node SDK differs from Go where we append `-retryN` to ids. Looks like parity gap.

marlene: also seeing OTEL_LOG_INJECTION=true causing trace_id to appear only after the first WARN. so some logs miss trace/span until later. that plus reused rid is making tracing impossible.

samir: two issues: (1) retry semantics: should either keep a stable top-level operation id and add an `attempt` field, or generate a new attempt-scoped id. (2) log level escalation: auth error path logs at WARN and that suppresses debug stack traces in log collection. Should log full debug then escalate summary to WARN.

devin: quick fix: change retry middleware to: `const attemptId = ctx.reqId ? ctx.reqId + '-a' + attempt : uuid()` and always include `attempt` field. That keeps correlation but makes attempts distinct.

alex: i prefer stable operation id + attempt number field. consumers often correlate on operation id. generating new id loses that. so implement `operation_id` and `attempt_id` fields. Also update docs for SDK parity.

marlene: redaction note: authorization header redactor currently does `s/(Bearer\s+)[A-Za-z0-9\-\._~\+\/]+=*/$1[REDACTED]/` which leaves `Bearer ` then `[REDACTED]`, and our second-pass redactor matches that pattern again and produces `Bearer [REDACTED]` twice in compound headers. We should anchor to header value only and early-out if `[REDACTED]` present.

samir: agree. make redactor idempotent and avoid matching the bracketed placeholder. unit test: run two-pass redaction and assert no change after first pass.

devin: also add a CI smoke test: start examples/node-starter with OTEL_LOG_INJECTION=true and REDWOOD_REDACT_PATTERNS set, run a scripted failing auth that triggers retry, then grep logs for `request_id=.* attempt=.*` and ensure operation_id stable + attempt increments, and assert no `request_id` repeated with different attempts. fail if pattern `request_id=.* attempt=1` and later same `request_id` and attempt=2.

rachel: i'll open PR that: (a) adds operation_id + attempt, (b) keeps existing reqid as operation_id for parity, (c) updates retry middleware and tests, (d) makes redactor idempotent and documents the authorization redaction caveat.

telemetry-bot: NOTE: created issue #4786 (devex) "node-starter: retry reuses request_id + loglevel escalation on auth retry; redaction idempotency" by rachel

alex: ping @eng-runtime for review since this affects startup and metrics. small follow-up: consider adding a config `RETRY_PRESERVE_OPERATION_ID=true` to let users opt-in to stable op ids if they rely on them.

samir: sounds good. rachel, drop repro snippet and test instructions in the issue. i'll help with Node SDK changes.

rachel: will do, thanks all :+1:
